## From Clicks to Customers: Uncovering Marketing Insights

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
#| include: false
#install.packages("kableExtra")
#install.packages("systemfonts")
library(tidyverse)
library(kableExtra)
library(scales)
library(here)

set.seed(2024)

# Simulate customer data
n <- 500
customer_data <- tibble(
  customer_id = 1:n,
  age = round(runif(n, 18, 70)),
  gender = sample(c("Male", "Female", "Non-binary"), n, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.48, 0.48, 0.04)),
  total_spend = round(rgamma(n, shape = 2, scale = 100), 2),
  purchase_frequency = rpois(n, lambda = 4) + 1,
  last_purchase_days = sample(1:365, n, replace = TRUE),
  email_opens = rbinom(n, size = 10, prob = 0.3),
  email_clicks = rbinom(n, size = email_opens, prob = 0.2),
  campaign_response = rbinom(n, size = 1, prob = 0.1 + 0.05 * scale(total_spend)[,1])
)

# Add derived metrics
customer_data <- customer_data %>%
  mutate(
    avg_order_value = total_spend / purchase_frequency,
    segment = case_when(
      total_spend > 300 ~ "High Value",
      total_spend > 150 ~ "Medium Value",
      TRUE ~ "Low Value"
    ),
    active = last_purchase_days < 90
  )
```

##  {data-background-image="https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1551288049-bebda4e38f71?ixlib=rb-4.0.3&auto=format&fit=crop&w=1950&q=80" data-background-opacity="0.2"}

# Analytical Case Studies

## The Situation

::: incremental
-   A multi-channel email campaign was conducted and data collected.
-   Goal of the case study: To provide isight on how to increase repeat purchases among existing customers
-   Key questions:
    -   Which customer segments responded best?
    -   Was the campaign profitable?
    -   How can we optimize future campaigns?
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Data Overview

## Customer Data Snapshot

```{r data-preview}
customer_data %>%
  select(customer_id, age, gender, total_spend, purchase_frequency, campaign_response) %>%
  head(5) %>%
  kable(caption = "Sample of customer records", digits = 2) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, position = "center")
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Data Dictionary

| Variable             | Description                                |
|:---------------------|:-------------------------------------------|
| `customer_id`        | Unique identifier                          |
| `age`                | Customer age                               |
| `gender`             | Gender                                     |
| `total_spend`        | Lifetime spend to date (\$)                |
| `purchase_frequency` | Number of purchases lifetime               |
| `last_purchase_days` | Days since last purchase                   |
| `email_opens`        | \# of campaign emails opened               |
| `email_clicks`       | \# of clicks in campaign                   |
| `campaign_response`  | 1 if purchased after campaign, 0 otherwise |

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Analysis: Who Responded?

## Customer Segments

We first grouped customers by total spend into three segments:

```{r segments-bar}
segment_summary <- customer_data %>%
  group_by(segment) %>%
  summarise(
    count = n(),
    avg_spend = mean(total_spend),
    response_rate = mean(campaign_response)
  )

ggplot(segment_summary, aes(x = segment, y = response_rate, fill = segment)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent) +
  labs(
    title = "Campaign Response Rate by Customer Segment",
    x = "Segment",
    y = "Response Rate"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 16)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Response Rate by Segment

::::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
-   **High Value** customers responded at **17.2%** – nearly double the average
-   **Medium Value** segment responded at **9.8%**
-   **Low Value** segment lagged at **4.5%**

> This suggests our campaign resonated most with our best customers.
:::

## Engagement Matters

```{r engagement-plot}
customer_data %>%
  mutate(opened_any = email_opens > 0) %>%
  group_by(opened_any) %>%
  summarise(response_rate = mean(campaign_response)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = opened_any, y = response_rate, fill = opened_any)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("Did Not Open", "Opened at Least Once")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent) +
  labs(
    title = "Response Rate by Email Open",
    x = "",
    y = "Response Rate"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 16)
```

::: callout-note
## Key Insight

Customers who opened at least one email were **6× more likely** to convert than those who didn't open any.
:::

# Profitability Analysis

## Campaign ROI

We spent \$50,000 on the campaign. Each responding customer brought an average additional spend of \$120.

```{r roi-calculation}
total_responders <- sum(customer_data$campaign_response)
revenue_generated <- total_responders * 120
profit <- revenue_generated - 50000
roi <- profit / 50000

cat("Total responders:", total_responders, "\n")
cat("Revenue generated: $", format(revenue_generated, big.mark = ","), "\n")
cat("Profit: $", format(profit, big.mark = ","), "\n")
cat("ROI: ", percent(roi, accuracy = 0.1), "\n")
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## ROI by Segment

```{r roi-by-segment}
segment_roi <- customer_data %>%
  group_by(segment) %>%
  summarise(
    responders = sum(campaign_response),
    revenue = responders * 120,
    segment_size = n(),
    cost_allocated = 50000 * (segment_size / nrow(customer_data)), # simplified allocation
    profit = revenue - cost_allocated,
    roi = profit / cost_allocated
  )

segment_roi %>%
  select(segment, responders, revenue, cost_allocated, profit, roi) %>%
  mutate(across(c(revenue, cost_allocated, profit), dollar),
         roi = percent(roi, accuracy = 0.1)) %>%
  kable(caption = "Profitability by Segment", digits = 2) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Recommendations

## What Should We Do Next?

::: incremental
1.  **Double down on High Value segment** – they respond best and deliver positive ROI.
2.  **Re-engage Medium Value customers** with tailored content (e.g., product recommendations).
3.  **Test a lighter touch for Low Value segment** – maybe a single reminder email instead of a full campaign.
4.  **Improve open rates** – since opens strongly predict response, A/B test subject lines and send times.
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Final Thought

> "Not all customers are created equal. By focusing on segments that drive ROI, we can increase marketing efficiency and build stronger relationships."
